sentences.text: Most species of Paraorthacodus are known only from isolated teeth featuring a single large central cusp with shorter lateral cusplets designed for clutching prey.
These teeth differ from those of Synechodus because their lateral cusplets decrease in size linearly rather than exponentially.
The species possessed a single dorsal fin located towards the rear of the body without a fin spine.
The genus Paraorthacodus was described by Glückman in 1957.
Fossils of P. jurensis from Late Jurassic Germany suggest juveniles had robust bodies with round heads, while adults had large fusiform profiles.
Paraorthacodus is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The parent group for Paraorthacodus is the family Palaeospinacidae.
Paraorthacodus belongs to the family Paraorthacodontidae, which is classified within either the order Hexanchiformes or Synechodontiformes.
The genus lived from the Hettangian to the Priabonian, approximately 201.4 to 33.9 million years ago.
The genus spans from the Early Jurassic to the Paleocene, or possibly the Eocene.
